Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

healthexpectancies 0.1.0

First version with a NEWS file. It lists the changes since version 0.0.0.9003 (November 2021).

New functions

  • fitPrevalenceModel() estimates a model of the evolution of prevalences of disability by age on past observations, and predict() projects prevalences from it. Three methods: extrapolation of the trend of prevalences at each age (method = "trend"), link with the evolution of mortality rates, with an age shift between disability and death that can be selected on a grid (method = "mortality"), and hypotheses on life expectancies (method = "target"): constant, linear trend or change of x percent at a given horizon of life expectancy with disability, disability-free life expectancy, their share in total life expectancy or their ratio, at each age (inversion of the Sullivan method) or uniformly at all ages from the value at one age (the minimum age, or anchor_age), with a common shift of the logit of prevalences or a common factor on prevalences (uniform_scale). At the youngest ages, where the inversion is unstable, from_age applies the hypothesis from a given age only.
  • fitPrevalenceModel(method = "shift"): horizontal shift of the curve of prevalences by age at a constant speed (in years of age per calendar year). The years used for the estimation are set with fit_years and exclude_years. The results of the estimation are available with coef(), fitted(), residuals(), summary() and as.data.frame(what = ...).
  • projectPrevalence() estimates, projects and calculates life expectancies in one step.

Datasets

  • New dataset FRAPAprevalence: prevalence of the APA by age bracket, 2010-2024 (source: DREES, via package asdep).
  • New datasets of Insee population projections: FRInseePopulationForecast2021 and FRInseePopulationForecast2026 (population by sex and age, central scenario, with observed values for past years).
  • New datasets of Insee mortality projections: FRInseeMortalityForecast2021 (observed values up to 2020, projections up to 2120) and FRInseeMortalityForecast2026 (observed values up to 2022, projections up to 2125).
  • New dataset FRInseeMortalityrates_t69: observed mortality rates by sex and age from Insee’s table T69, as an alternative to FRInseeMortalityrates.
  • New dataset FRDreesVQSsurvey2021: prevalences of disabilities by sex and age bracket from the 2021 Vie quotidienne et santé survey.
  • New dataset FRGaliEUSilc: prevalence of general activity limitations (GALI) by sex and age bracket, from the SRCV survey (French part of EU-SILC), updated up to 2024.
  • New dataset FRDreesEHPA: share of people living in institutions for older people by sex and age, from the EHPA surveys (2007 to 2023).
  • Updated datasets: FRDreesAPA (years 2016 to 2024, by sex and age), FRInseePopulation and FRInseeMortalityrates (versions of January 2026). Error corrected in FRInseeMortalityForecast2026.

Changes

  • prevalenceApprox() and ApproxPrevalenceTable() now smooth prevalences by age on the logit scale, which guarantees prevalences between 0 and 1 and removes a strong underestimation of prevalences at the first ages (more than 50 percent at the minimum age with the former method). Use method = "legacy" (option = "legacy" in ApproxPrevalenceTable()) to get earlier results. Prevalences must now be proportions between 0 and 1 (not percentages) with the default method.
  • ApproxPrevalenceTable() identifies age brackets from the variable ‘age’ (numbers or labels such as “[60,65)”), sorts rows by age, checks them against agecuts and the weights against the range of ages, and returns explicit error messages that name the series concerned.
  • prevalenceForecast() checks its arguments and has a new argument on_unfeasible that sets what to do when a hypothesis would require prevalences outside the interval 0 to 1 (“warn”, “clip” or “error”).
  • CompleteDFLEtable(): missing values are handled group by group, with a single warning (columns entirely NA are treated as absent); the share of life expectancy lived at age 0 only uses the 0.2 coefficient of the Sullivan manual at age 0; variables defining categories are restored in all cases.
  • Packages matlib, shiny, shinydashboard and plotly are no longer required to install the package; tidyr and stringr, used by the code, are now declared.
  • Tests (testthat) have been added.
  • projectPrevalence() warns when the model does not cover all the ages of the life table given in newdata (life expectancies would then be calculated with a life table that stops at the last age of the model).
  • Shiny app (runExample()): prevalences by single year of age are now smoothed with prevalenceApprox() (logit of prevalences) instead of a polynomial approximation, which could give negative prevalences; hypotheses that would require prevalences outside the interval 0 to 1 are bounded (on_unfeasible = "clip").
  • The package passes R CMD check without errors or warnings (non-ASCII characters removed from the code, variables of dplyr pipelines declared, files ignored when building the package).

Documentation

  • New vignette “Methods for projecting prevalences” describing the methods of fitPrevalenceModel(), with an application to the APA.
  • The vignette “how-to-use-healthexpectancies” is replaced by “Getting started with healthexpectancies”, a tutorial with executed examples of the main functions and an overview of the datasets.
  • README and pkgdown website updated.
  • Citation: citation("healthexpectancies") (file inst/CITATION) and CITATION.cff file for GitHub and Zenodo.

Bug fixes

  • Functions failed in a session where the tidyverse was not attached: imports are now declared.
  • prevalenceForecast() with hypothesis cstPctDLE did not work.
  • Shiny app (runExample()): the default hypothesis (constant prevalences) stopped with an error, since it used an obsolete name of the hypothesis.
  • Examples of prevalenceApprox() failed when dplyr was not attached; they now use base R only.
  • prevalence_to_polynomial(): typo (False instead of FALSE) in the expansion of prevalences by age bracket.
  • Documentation of the dataset sullivan: all variables are now described.
  • CompleteDFLEtable(): mean, median and modal ages of disability returned Inf (with a warning) when prevalences were negative; they are now NA.
